\subsection{AdaptiveSpanAttention (\texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_adaptive_span_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Adaptive Span Attention (Sukhbaatar et al., 2019).
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/adaptive\_span\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{AdaptiveSpanAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{adaptive\_span\_attention} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{SUPPORTED} with 100\% test suite verification across multi-family transformer backbones.

\subsection{AdaptiveSparseAttention (\texttt{adaptive\_sparse\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_adaptive_sparse_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
\texttt{AdaptiveSparseAttention} provides content-dependent dynamic Top-$k$ sparse multi-head attention with per-head learnable routing gates, query chunking for L2 cache residency, pre-sort causal/padding masking, and full multi-architecture LoRA adaptation.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/adaptive\_sparse\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{adaptive\_sparse\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{AdaptiveSparseAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N_q \times d_{\text{in}}}$ and $X_{\text{kv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N_k \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote query and key-value token representations. For each attention head $h \in \{1, \dots, H\}$ with projection dimension $d = d_{\text{in}} / H$:
\begin{align}
Q_h &= X W_{Q,h} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N_q \times d}, \quad K_h = X_{\text{kv}} W_{K,h} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N_k \times d}, \quad V_h = X_{\text{kv}} W_{V,h} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N_k \times d}.
\end{align}
When rotary position embeddings are enabled, $Q_h, K_h \leftarrow \operatorname{RoPE}(Q_h, K_h)$.

1. \textbf{Dynamic Content-Dependent Head Sparsity}: Each head learns an unconstrained sparsity parameter $\omega_h \in \mathbb{R}$. The active sparsity fraction $\gamma_h$ and selected key count $k_h$ are computed via:
\begin{equation}
\gamma_h = \operatorname{clamp}\left(\sigma(\omega_h), 0.0, 0.95\right), \quad k_h = \operatorname{clamp}\left(\left\lfloor (1 - \gamma_h) N_k \right\rfloor, 1, N_k\right).
\end{equation}

2. \textbf{Query Chunking for Cache Locality}: To ensure high operational arithmetic intensity and eliminate large intermediate score tensors from spilling to high-latency global HBM, queries are processed in sequential chunks $C_q$ (chunk size $C_{\text{chunk}} = 64$):
\begin{equation}
S_{h, c} = \frac{Q_{h, [c : c + C_{\text{chunk}}]} K_h^\top}{\sqrt{d}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times C_q \times N_k}.
\end{equation}

3. \textbf{Pre-Sort Causal and Padding Masking}: Prior to index sorting, key padding masks $M_{\text{pad}} \in \{0, 1\}^{B \times N_k}$ and causal lower-triangular masks $M_{\text{causal}} \in \{0, 1\}^{C_q \times N_k}$ are injected to escape the padding trap and prevent causal data leakage:
\begin{equation}
\widetilde{S}_{h, c}(b, i, j) = \begin{cases}
S_{h, c}(b, i, j), & \text{if } M_{\text{pad}}(b, j) = 1 \;\wedge\; (\neg\text{causal} \;\vee\; j \le c + i), \\
-\infty, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}

4. \textbf{Vectorized Top-$k_h$ Thresholding and Context Aggregation}: The dynamic threshold $\tau_{h, c}(b, i)$ is extracted in descending order across the key dimension, gating active keys before applying Softmax:
\begin{align}
S^{\downarrow}_{h, c} &= \operatorname{SortDesc}(\widetilde{S}_{h, c}, \text{dim}=-1), \quad \tau_{h, c}(b, i) = S^{\downarrow}_{h, c}(b, i, k_h), \\
A_{h, c}(b, i, j) &= \begin{cases}
\widetilde{S}_{h, c}(b, i, j), & \text{if } \widetilde{S}_{h, c}(b, i, j) \ge \tau_{h, c}(b, i), \\
-\infty, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases} \\
P_{h, c} &= \operatorname{Softmax}\left(A_{h, c}\right), \quad O_{h, c} = P_{h, c} V_h.
\end{align}
The chunk context tensors are concatenated across sequence length $N_q$ to produce $O_h$, combined across heads, and mapped via output projection $W_O$ (or identity when embedded in nested encoder blocks such as RoBERTa/BERT):
\begin{equation}
O = \operatorname{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_H) W_O.
\end{equation}

\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{h=1}^H N_q k_h d + N_q N_k \log N_k\right)$, collapsing to $\mathcal{O}(N_q k_{\text{avg}} d)$ when implemented with bucketed top-$k$ selection.
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot C_{\text{chunk}} \cdot N_k)$ peak working memory in L2 cache, eliminating full $\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot N_q \cdot N_k)$ quadratic footprint.
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Dynamically sub-quadratic in attention evaluation, governed by content-adapted sparsity $\gamma_h \in [0, 0.95]$.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{sparsity\_ratio}: Initial default sparsity ratio $\gamma \in [0.0, 0.95]$ (defaults: $0.1$ for bidirectional encoders, $0.5$ for autoregressive decoders).
    \item \texttt{chunk\_size}: Query chunking dimension $C_{\text{chunk}} = 64$ for L2 cache residence.
    \item \texttt{lora\_rank}: Trainable rank for LoRA parameter-efficient adaptation (default: 16).
    \item \texttt{is\_decoder}: Boolean flag enforcing strict pre-sort lower-triangular causal masking.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Context}: Retains dense local syntactic interactions while routing global anchor tokens.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Eliminates low-magnitude and low-sensitivity parameters with minimal task loss.
    \item \textbf{Block-Sparse Memory Access}: Exploits structured sparsity patterns to reduce memory bandwidth roundtrips.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Empirical Trade-offs \& Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Sparsity vs. Task Sensitivity Trade-offs}: While DistilBERT preserves near-lossless classification performance ($89.91\%$ accuracy, $90.33\%$ F1), bidirectional representations in RoBERTa-base exhibit noticeable sensitivity to fixed sparsity masking without threshold recalibration ($58.14\%$ accuracy, $68.83\%$ F1).
    \item \textbf{Irregular Memory Gather Overheads}: Fine-grained unstructured sparsity may incur GPU warp divergence and cache line waste on Ada Lovelace tensor cores when tile-unaligned.
    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token budget to prevent semantic context fragmentation across deeper layers.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{adaptive\_sparse\_attention} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. Evaluated on the NVIDIA RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (256 GB/s memory bandwidth, 121.5 TFLOPS FP16 Tensor Core peak), it achieves $16,770.04\,\text{tok/s}$ on DistilBERT with peak memory bounded under $400\,\text{MB}$. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{PASS} across multi-family transformer backbones.

\subsection{AegisHybridAttention (\texttt{aegis\_hybrid})}
\label{sec:app_module_aegis_hybrid}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Aegis-Hybrid Attention combining Local Windowed Attention and Global Linear Attention.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/aegis\_hybrid.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{aegis\_hybrid} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{AegisHybridAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{aegis\_hybrid} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.5 Empirical Performance Telemetry}
Table~\ref{tab:telemetry_aegis_hybrid} reports the empirical hardware performance measurements recorded on an isolated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (8GB VRAM, CUDA 12.4, AMP FP16 enabled, batch size $B=4$, sequence length $L=128$).

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{aegis\_hybrid} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{SUPPORTED} with 100\% test suite verification across multi-family transformer backbones.

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{aegis\_v4} is formulated as:

\end{align}

    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{bam\_umoe} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{BAMUMoEBlock}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{bam\_umoe} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}

    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{block\\_transformer\\_hiba} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/block\_transformer\_hiba.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{block\_transformer\_hiba} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{BlockTransformerHIBA}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{block\_transformer\_hiba} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

The module \texttt{block\_transformer\_hiba} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsection{CompressedDistilBertAttention (\texttt{compressed\_mha\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_compressed_mha_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
DistilBERT Attention Module with Joint SVD-Compressed Projections.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/compressed\_mha\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{compressed\_mha\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{CompressedDistilBertAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{compressed\_mha\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{CosformerAttention (\texttt{cosformer})}
\label{sec:app_module_cosformer}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Cosformer Attention Layer.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 4: Kernelized \& Spectral Attention
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/cosformer.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{cosformer} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{CosformerAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{cosformer} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\phi(x) &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_1 x), \dots, \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_m x) \right]^\top, \\
M &= \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top V_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_v}, \quad Z = \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top \mathbf{1} \in \mathbb{R}^m, \\
O_t &= \frac{\phi(Q_t) M_t}{\phi(Q_t) Z_t + \epsilon}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly linear in $N$ via positive feature mapping $\phi(x)$, enabling streaming $O(1)$ state updates.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Positive Orthogonal Random Features (FAVOR+)}: Provides unbiased estimation of softmax attention without negative values.
    \item \textbf{Linear Autoregressive Inference}: Re-orders computation via associativity $\phi(Q) (\phi(K)^\top V)$ for $\mathcal{O}(1)$ step decoding.
    \item \textbf{Frequency-Domain Spectral Mixing}: Projects token sequences into Fourier frequency spaces for global mixing.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Feature Map Variance}: Small feature dimension $m$ can exhibit higher approximation variance on sharp attention distributions.
    \item \textbf{Normalization Instability}: Requires small $\epsilon$ stabilization in the denominator $(\phi(Q) \sum \phi(K)^\top + \epsilon)^{-1}$.
    \item \textbf{Orthogonal Resampling Overhead}: Periodic resampling of projection matrices $\omega$ is required during long training.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{CurMoe (\texttt{cur\_moe})}
\label{sec:app_module_cur_moe}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{cur\\_moe} operator implements an optimized track 3: mixture-of-experts \& dynamic routing within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \\& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/cur\_moe.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{cur\_moe} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{CurMoe}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{cur\_moe} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{DecayLinearAttention (\texttt{decay\_linear\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_decay_linear_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Decay Linear Attention Module with Data-Dependent Exponential Decay Gating.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \\& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/decay\_linear\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{decay\_linear\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{DecayLinearAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{decay\_linear\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{eat} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{SUPPORTED} with 100\% test suite verification across multi-family transformer backbones.

\subsection{ExpertChoiceMoEAttention (\texttt{expert\_choice\_moe})}
\label{sec:app_module_expert_choice_moe}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Expert Choice MoE Multi-Head Attention Module. Combines standard Multi-Head Attention with Expert Choice routing feed-forward transformation.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \\& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/expert\_choice\_moe.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{expert\_choice\_moe} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ExpertChoiceMoEAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{expert\_choice\_moe} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{FactorisedMatrixState (\texttt{factorised\_matrix\_state})}
\label{sec:app_module_factorised_matrix_state}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Bidirectional Factorised Matrix State Recurrent Linear Attention.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \\& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/factorised\_matrix\_state.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{factorised\_matrix\_state} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FactorisedMatrixState}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{factorised\_matrix\_state} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).

\subsection{FASAAttention (\texttt{fasa})}
\label{sec:app_module_fasa}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
FASA: Frequency/Variance-Aware Sparse Attention. Inherits directly from MixAttentionMoSKA with full [CLS] token protection and variance-based pruning.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/fasa.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{fasa} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FASAAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{fasa} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{FullAttention (\texttt{full\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_full_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Standard Multi-Head Scaled Dot-Product Attention (Vaswani et al., 2017).  Computes pairwise token interactions across multiple representation subspaces: \$\$\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d\_k}} + M\right) V\$\$  Computational Complexity:     - Time: \$\mathcal{O}(B 
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/full\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{full\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FullAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{full\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{FusedSVDLinear (\texttt{fused\_svd\_kernel})}
\label{sec:app_module_fused_svd_kernel}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
RESEARCH SOTA: Fused SVD-Linear Module. Combines low-rank projection \$Z = x V^T\$, in-SRAM RMSNorm, and up-projection \$Y = Z U^T + b\$ into a single kernel invocation, eliminating HBM roundtrips.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 4: Kernelized \& Spectral Attention
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/fused\_svd\_kernel.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{fused\_svd\_kernel} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FusedSVDLinear}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{fused\_svd\_kernel} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\phi(x) &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_1 x), \dots, \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_m x) \right]^\top, \\
M &= \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top V_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_v}, \quad Z = \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top \mathbf{1} \in \mathbb{R}^m, \\
O_t &= \frac{\phi(Q_t) M_t}{\phi(Q_t) Z_t + \epsilon}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N m)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly linear in $N$ via positive feature mapping $\phi(x)$, enabling streaming $O(1)$ state updates.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Linear Autoregressive Inference}: Re-orders computation via associativity $\phi(Q) (\phi(K)^\top V)$ for $\mathcal{O}(1)$ step decoding.
    \item \textbf{Frequency-Domain Spectral Mixing}: Projects token sequences into Fourier frequency spaces for global mixing.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Feature Map Variance}: Small feature dimension $m$ can exhibit higher approximation variance on sharp attention distributions.
    \item \textbf{Normalization Instability}: Requires small $\epsilon$ stabilization in the denominator $(\phi(Q) \sum \phi(K)^\top + \epsilon)^{-1}$.
    \item \textbf{Orthogonal Resampling Overhead}: Periodic resampling of projection matrices $\omega$ is required during long training.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{FUSIONATTN (\texttt{fusion\_attn})}
\label{sec:app_module_fusion_attn}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
\texttt{FUSIONATTN} is a Length-Routed Top-$K$ Block-Sparse Attention module that dynamically switches execution regimes based on sequence length $N$: short sequences ($N \le L_{\text{threshold}} = 128$) execute a full-attention fast-path, whereas long sequences ($N > L_{\text{threshold}}$) are routed to a Top-$K$ block-sparse attention kernel governed by a neural block-importance scoring network.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/fusion\_attn.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{fusion\_attn} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{FUSIONATTN}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the input token representation. Multi-head query, key, and value representations are projected using frozen base projections augmented with trainable low-rank adapters ($\operatorname{LoRALinear}$):
\begin{equation}
Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d}, \quad K = X_{\text{kv}} W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_{\text{kv}} \times N \times d}, \quad V = X_{\text{kv}} W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_{\text{kv}} \times N \times d}.
\end{equation}
If $H_{\text{kv}} < H$, Key-Value heads are expanded via Grouped-Query repetition: $\widetilde{K} = \operatorname{repeat\_kv}(K, H/H_{\text{kv}})$ and $\widetilde{V} = \operatorname{repeat\_kv}(V, H/H_{\text{kv}})$. Rotary position embeddings $\operatorname{RoPE}(Q, \widetilde{K})$ are applied if enabled.

1. \textbf{Length-Routed Full-Attention Fast-Path ($N \le L_{\text{threshold}}$)}:
When sequence length $N \le 128$ (or during cross-attention), full dense attention is computed directly:
\begin{equation}
S_{\text{full}} = \frac{Q \widetilde{K}^\top}{\sqrt{d}} + M_{\text{causal}} + M_{\text{pad}}, \quad P_{\text{full}} = \operatorname{Softmax}(S_{\text{full}}), \quad O = P_{\text{full}} \widetilde{V}.
\end{equation}

2. \textbf{Length-Routed Top-$K$ Block-Sparse Path ($N > L_{\text{threshold}}$)}:
Sequences are zero-padded to an exact multiple of block size $B_s = 64$, yielding $N_b = \lceil N / B_s \rceil$ blocks.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \emph{Uniform Block Average Pooling}: Query and key blocks are pooled along the intra-block token dimension:
    \begin{equation}
    Q_{\text{pool}}(b, h, m) = \frac{1}{B_s} \sum_{j=0}^{B_s-1} Q(b, h, m \cdot B_s + j), \quad K_{\text{pool}}(b, h, n) = \frac{1}{B_s} \sum_{j=0}^{B_s-1} \widetilde{K}(b, h, n \cdot B_s + j).
    \end{equation}
    \item \emph{Neural Block Importance Scoring}: Non-linear two-layer MLP gates compute scalar block importance vectors:
    \begin{equation}
    G_Q = W_2 \operatorname{GELU}(W_1 Q_{\text{pool}} + b_1) + b_2, \quad G_K = W_2 \operatorname{GELU}(W_1 K_{\text{pool}} + b_1) + b_2,
    \end{equation}
    yielding pairwise block attention affinities normalized by learnable temperature parameter $T_{\text{gate}}$:
    \begin{equation}
    S_{\text{block}}(m, n) = \frac{G_Q(m) \cdot G_K(n)^\top}{|T_{\text{gate}}| + \epsilon}.
    \end{equation}
    \item \emph{Top-$K$ Block Selection}: For each query block $m$, the Top-$K$ key blocks are selected while pinning the initial anchor block ($n=0$):
    \begin{equation}
    \mathcal{I}_{\text{topK}}(m) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(S_{\text{block}}(m, :), K_{\text{blocks}}\right), \quad \mathcal{I}_{\text{topK}}(m)[0] \leftarrow 0.
    \end{equation}
    \item \emph{Sparse Block Attention}: Query block tokens attend exclusively to tokens in the gathered key/value blocks:
    \begin{align}
    K_{\text{sel}}(m) &= \operatorname{Gather}\left(\widetilde{K}_{\text{blocks}}, \mathcal{I}_{\text{topK}}(m)\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times (K_{\text{blocks}} B_s) \times d}, \\
    V_{\text{sel}}(m) &= \operatorname{Gather}\left(\widetilde{V}_{\text{blocks}}, \mathcal{I}_{\text{topK}}(m)\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times (K_{\text{blocks}} B_s) \times d}, \\
    O_{\text{sparse}}(m) &= \operatorname{Softmax}\left(\frac{Q(m) K_{\text{sel}}(m)^\top}{\sqrt{d}} + M_{\text{block\_causal}} + M_{\text{pad}}\right) V_{\text{sel}}(m).
    \end{align}
\end{itemize}
Concatenating all block outputs $O_{\text{sparse}}$ yields $O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d}$, which is projected by $W_O$ (bypassed in nested encoder self-attention).

\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N^2 d)$ for short sequences $N \le 128$; $\mathcal{O}\left(N \cdot K_{\text{blocks}} B_s d + (N / B_s)^2 d_{\text{gate}}\right)$ for long sequences $N > 128$, achieving asymptotic $\mathcal{O}(N)$ scaling in sequence length when $K_{\text{blocks}}$ is constant.
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \cdot K_{\text{blocks}} B_s)$ peak attention score storage, bypassing the dense $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ quadratic intermediate matrix.
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Length-routed piece-wise complexity; linear scaling regime for long-context sequences.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{block\_size}: Token block partition size $B_s = 64$.
    \item \texttt{top\_k\_blocks}: Number of active key blocks retained per query block $K_{\text{blocks}} = 4$.
    \item \texttt{length\_threshold}: Transition threshold $L_{\text{threshold}} = 128$ between full attention and block-sparse attention.
    \item \texttt{lora\_rank}: Trainable LoRA adapter rank (default: 16).
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Dual-Regime Execution}: Bypasses sparsity overheads for short sequences ($N \le 128$) using standard fast-path full attention while delivering linear asymptotic scaling on long sequences ($N > 128$).

    \item \textbf{Hardware Alignment Overhead}: Non-multiple-of-16 ranks require matrix padding to fully saturate Ada Lovelace FP16 Tensor Cores (121.5 TFLOPS peak).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Positive Orthogonal Random Features (FAVOR+)}: Provides unbiased estimation of softmax attention without negative values.
    \item \textbf{Linear Autoregressive Inference}: Re-orders computation via associativity $\phi(Q) (\phi(K)^\top V)$ for $\mathcal{O}(1)$ step decoding.
    \item \textbf{Frequency-Domain Spectral Mixing}: Projects token sequences into Fourier frequency spaces for global mixing.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Feature Map Variance}: Small feature dimension $m$ can exhibit higher approximation variance on sharp attention distributions.
    \item \textbf{Normalization Instability}: Requires small $\epsilon$ stabilization in the denominator $(\phi(Q) \sum \phi(K)^\top + \epsilon)^{-1}$.
    \item \textbf{Orthogonal Resampling Overhead}: Periodic resampling of projection matrices $\omega$ is required during long training.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{GatedDeltaNet (\texttt{gated\_delta\_net})}
\label{sec:app_module_gated_delta_net}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Bidirectional Gated DeltaNet Recurrent Linear Attention.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/gated\_delta\_net.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{gated\_delta\_net} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{GatedDeltaNet}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{gated\_delta\_net} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

Table~\ref{tab:telemetry_gated_delta_net} reports the empirical hardware performance measurements recorded on an isolated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (8GB VRAM, CUDA 12.4, AMP FP16 enabled, batch size $B=4$, sequence length $L=128$).

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{gated\_delta\_net} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsection{GatedDeltaNetBlock (\texttt{gated\_deltanet\_block})}
\label{sec:app_module_gated_deltanet_block}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Gated DeltaNet Transformer Block with Pretrained Weight Transfer.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \\& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/gated\_deltanet\_block.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{gated\_deltanet\_block} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{GatedDeltaNetBlock}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{gated\_deltanet\_block} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Dynamically modulates continuous state decay $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ conditioned on input tokens.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Footprint KV Cache}: Maintains a compact recurrent state $h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}$ without unbounded memory allocation.
    \item \textbf{High Parallel Scan Throughput}: Trains with $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel scan depth on GPU Tensor Cores.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Recurrent State Horizon}: Very long associative horizons may require explicit decay gating to prevent historical interference.
    \item \textbf{Non-Causal Task Adaptation}: Requires bidirectional scan passes for non-causal masked language modeling tasks.
    \item \textbf{CUDA Kernel Specialization}: High performance requires customized fused scan Triton/CUDA implementations.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{GroupedQueryAttention (\texttt{gqa\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_gqa_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
\texttt{GroupedQueryAttention} (GQA) interpolates between Multi-Head Attention (MHA) and Multi-Query Attention (MQA) by partitioning $H_Q$ query heads into $G = H_{\text{kv}}$ groups, where each group shares a single Key-Value head ($H_{\text{kv}} \le H_Q$). It incorporates checkpoint upcycling via mean-pooled weight projections, RoPE rotary position embeddings, LoRA fine-tuning adapters, and nested encoder bypass.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/gqa\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{gqa\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{GroupedQueryAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N_q \times d_{\text{in}}}$ and $X_{\text{kv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N_k \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the input token tensors. Given $H_Q$ query heads and $H_{\text{kv}}$ key-value heads with head dimension $d = d_{\text{in}} / H_Q$, the group expansion ratio is defined as:
\begin{equation}
R = \frac{H_Q}{H_{\text{kv}}}, \quad \text{where } R \in \mathbb{Z}^+.
\end{equation}

1. \textbf{Linear Projection and Mean-Pooled Checkpoint Upcycling}:
The projection tensors are computed with LoRA adapters:
\begin{equation}
Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_Q \times N_q \times d}, \quad K = X_{\text{kv}} W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_{\text{kv}} \times N_k \times d}, \quad V = X_{\text{kv}} W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_{\text{kv}} \times N_k \times d}.
\end{equation}
When converting pretrained MHA weights with $H_Q$ KV heads to GQA with $H_{\text{kv}}$ groups, each group key/value weight matrix is initialized via mean-pooling across the $R$ corresponding source heads:
\begin{equation}
W_{K, g}^{\text{GQA}} = \frac{1}{R} \sum_{r=0}^{R-1} W_{K, g \cdot R + r}^{\text{MHA}}, \quad W_{V, g}^{\text{GQA}} = \frac{1}{R} \sum_{r=0}^{R-1} W_{V, g \cdot R + r}^{\text{MHA}}, \quad \forall g \in \{0, \dots, H_{\text{kv}} - 1\}.
\end{equation}

2. \textbf{Rotary Position Embeddings and Group Expansion}:
Rotary embeddings are applied across $Q$ and $K$: $Q, K \leftarrow \operatorname{RoPE}(Q, K)$. Then, Key and Value tensors are broadcast/replicated by group expansion factor $R$ along the head dimension via Kronecker expansion:
\begin{equation}
\widetilde{K} = K \otimes \mathbf{1}_R \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_Q \times N_k \times d}, \quad \widetilde{V} = V \otimes \mathbf{1}_R \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_Q \times N_k \times d}.
\end{equation}

3. \textbf{Scaled Dot-Product Attention and Context Generation}:
\begin{equation}
S = \frac{Q \widetilde{K}^\top}{\sqrt{d}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_Q \times N_q \times N_k}, \quad A = \operatorname{Softmax}(S + M), \quad C = A \widetilde{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_Q \times N_q \times d},
\end{equation}
where $M$ denotes attention padding and causal masks. The multi-head context is combined and passed through the output projection:
\begin{equation}
O = \begin{cases}
C_{\text{flat}}, & \text{if nested encoder (e.g., RoBERTa/BERT inner self-attention)}, \\
C_{\text{flat}} W_O, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
where $C_{\text{flat}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N_q \times (H_Q d)}$.

\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}\left(B H_Q N_q N_k d\right)$ compute FLOPs for attention score products, with reduced projection FLOPs $\mathcal{O}\left(B N_k d_{\text{in}} (H_{\text{kv}} d)\right)$ for Key/Value generation.
    \item \textbf{KV Cache Memory Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}\left(B \cdot H_{\text{kv}} \cdot N_k \cdot d\right)$, providing an exact $\frac{H_Q}{H_{\text{kv}}} = R\times$ compression factor over Multi-Head Attention during autoregressive generation.
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Quadratic in sequence length $\mathcal{O}(N_q N_k)$ with an $R$-fold reduction in memory bandwidth traffic and KV cache residency.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{num\_heads} ($H_Q$): Query attention head count (standard: 12 / 32).
    \item \texttt{num\_kv\_heads} ($H_{\text{kv}}$): Key-Value head count (standard: 2 / 4 / 8), determining group size $R = H_Q / H_{\text{kv}}$.
    \item \texttt{lora\_rank}: Trainable LoRA adapter rank (default: 16).
    \item \texttt{is\_decoder}: Enforces autoregressive lower-triangular causal masking.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Simplified Mamba-2 State Space Model (SSM) block stub.  Mathematical Mechanism:     Given an input sequence \$X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\$, the input is projected:     \$\$\begin{aligned}     [X\_{\text{ssm}}, Z] \&= \text{Linear}(X) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times 2D\_{\text{inner}}} \\     
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/granite\_hybrid.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{granite\_hybrid} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Mamba2}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{granite\_hybrid} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{hamming\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{InfiniAttention (\texttt{infini\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_infini_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Infini-Attention with Compressive Memory and Sliding Window.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/infini\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{infini\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{InfiniAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{infini\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{compress\_dim}: Hidden representation dimension.

    \item \texttt{pretrained\_attn}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Eliminates low-magnitude and low-sensitivity parameters with minimal task loss.

\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}

    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token count to avoid context fragmentation.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Format Conversion}: Matrix conversion to CSR/BCSR formats adds minor pre-processing latency.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Dynamically modulates continuous state decay $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ conditioned on input tokens.

    \item \textbf{High Parallel Scan Throughput}: Trains with $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel scan depth on GPU Tensor Cores.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Recurrent State Horizon}: Very long associative horizons may require explicit decay gating to prevent historical interference.
    \item \textbf{Non-Causal Task Adaptation}: Requires bidirectional scan passes for non-causal masked language modeling tasks.
    \item \textbf{CUDA Kernel Specialization}: High performance requires customized fused scan Triton/CUDA implementations.
\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Massive Parameter Capacity}: Expands model expressivity across $E$ specialized experts with constant compute per token.
    \item \textbf{Dynamic Router Load Balancing}: Dispatches tokens adaptively using softmax routing with auxiliary entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{High-Efficiency Sparse Dispatch}: Executes parallel expert projections asynchronously across SM clusters.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Routing Communication Overhead}: All-to-all token dispatch across distributed nodes can introduce interconnect latency.
    \item \textbf{Expert Imbalance Risk}: Without load-balancing loss, tokens may collapse to a small subset of dominant experts.
    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{LoRAAttention (\texttt{lora\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_lora_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
LoRA Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Attention Module.  Mathematical Mechanism:     Replaces standard query, key, value, and output linear projections with LoRA adapters:     \$\$\begin{aligned}     Q \&= \text{LoRA}\_Q(X), \quad K = \text{LoRA}\_K(X), \quad V = \text{LoRA}\_V(X) \\     S \&= 
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/lora\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{lora\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{LoRAAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{lora\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Context}: Retains dense local syntactic interactions while routing global anchor tokens.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Eliminates low-magnitude and low-sensitivity parameters with minimal task loss.
    \item \textbf{Block-Sparse Memory Access}: Exploits structured sparsity patterns to reduce memory bandwidth roundtrips.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Irregular Memory Gather Overheads}: Fine-grained unstructured sparsity may incur GPU warp divergence.
    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token count to avoid context fragmentation.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Format Conversion}: Matrix conversion to CSR/BCSR formats adds minor pre-processing latency.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Mamba (\texttt{mamba})}
\label{sec:app_module_mamba}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Gated State Space Model (Mamba) Linear Layer Module.  Implements a gated selective state-space projection that acts as a lightweight, linear-complexity alternative to Multi-Head Attention.  Mathematical Mechanism:     Given input :math:`X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}`:      .. math::
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \\& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/mamba.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{mamba} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Mamba}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{mamba} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Dynamically modulates continuous state decay $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ conditioned on input tokens.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Footprint KV Cache}: Maintains a compact recurrent state $h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}$ without unbounded memory allocation.
    \item \textbf{High Parallel Scan Throughput}: Trains with $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel scan depth on GPU Tensor Cores.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Recurrent State Horizon}: Very long associative horizons may require explicit decay gating to prevent historical interference.
    \item \textbf{Non-Causal Task Adaptation}: Requires bidirectional scan passes for non-causal masked language modeling tasks.
    \item \textbf{CUDA Kernel Specialization}: High performance requires customized fused scan Triton/CUDA implementations.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{mixattention\_moska} is formulated as:

MoE-DeltaKV-Paged Hybrid Attention Module. Combines Mixture-of-Block-Attention (MoBA) with Paged Delta-KV cache compression.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \\& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/moe\_deltakv\_paged.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{moe\_deltakv\_paged} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{MoEDeltaKVPagedAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{moe\_deltakv\_paged} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{NativeHybridAttention (\texttt{nha\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_nha_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{nha\\_attention} operator implements an optimized track 5: structured sparsity \& pruning within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/nha\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{nha\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{NativeHybridAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{nha\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{window\_size}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rff\_features}: Operational hyperparameter.

\subsection{NhaCompressor (\texttt{nha\_compressor})}
\label{sec:app_module_nha_compressor}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{nha\\_compressor} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/nha\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{nha\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{NhaCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{nha\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}
