\subsection{NativeSparseAttention (\texttt{nsa\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_nsa_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Native Sparse Attention layer combining local windowing and global top-\$k\$ selection.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \\& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/nsa\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{nsa\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{NativeSparseAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{nsa\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{window\_size}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{top\_k}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{pretrained\_attn}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Massive Parameter Capacity}: Expands model expressivity across $E$ specialized experts with constant compute per token.
    \item \textbf{Dynamic Router Load Balancing}: Dispatches tokens adaptively using softmax routing with auxiliary entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{High-Efficiency Sparse Dispatch}: Executes parallel expert projections asynchronously across SM clusters.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Routing Communication Overhead}: All-to-all token dispatch across distributed nodes can introduce interconnect latency.
    \item \textbf{Expert Imbalance Risk}: Without load-balancing loss, tokens may collapse to a small subset of dominant experts.
    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{nsa\_attention} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsection{NystromAttention (\texttt{nystrom\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_nystrom_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Nyströmformer: Linear Complexity Self-Attention via Nyström Landmark Approximation (Xiong et al., 2021).
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/nystrom\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{nystrom\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{NystromAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{nystrom\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{num\_landmarks}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{pinv\_iterations}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{pretrained\_attn}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Context}: Retains dense local syntactic interactions while routing global anchor tokens.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Eliminates low-magnitude and low-sensitivity parameters with minimal task loss.
    \item \textbf{Block-Sparse Memory Access}: Exploits structured sparsity patterns to reduce memory bandwidth roundtrips.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Irregular Memory Gather Overheads}: Fine-grained unstructured sparsity may incur GPU warp divergence.
    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token count to avoid context fragmentation.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Format Conversion}: Matrix conversion to CSR/BCSR formats adds minor pre-processing latency.
\end{itemize}

\label{sec:app_module_phantom}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
PHANTOM Attention module with CUR factorized projections and multi-round LSH attention.  Args:     config (Optional[Any]): Transformer configuration object.     rank (Optional[int]): Compression rank.     phantom\_cfg (Optional[PHANTOMConfig]): PHANTOMConfig instance.     pretrained\_attn (Optional[An
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \\& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/phantom.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{phantom} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{PHANTOMAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{phantom} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{PrimalAttention (\texttt{primal\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_primal_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
\texttt{PrimalAttention} implements a Primal-Space Nystr\"om kernel approximation of self-attention using uniform segment landmark pooling, triple kernel submatrix construction ($F_1, F_2, F_3$), high-precision Moore-Penrose pseudoinversion in FP32 with condition cutoff $\text{rcond}=10^{-4}$, and iterative quadratic Schulz-Newton refinement. It natively supports RoPE positional embeddings, Grouped-Query repetition, LoRA adapters, and nested encoder bypass.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/primal\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{primal\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{PrimalAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the input token representation. Multi-head query, key, and value representations $Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d}$ and $K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_{\text{kv}} \times N \times d}$ are computed with $\operatorname{LoRALinear}$ adapters and expanded to $H$ heads via $\operatorname{repeat\_kv}$ when $H_{\text{kv}} < H$. If RoPE embeddings are active, $Q, K \leftarrow \operatorname{RoPE}(Q, K)$.

1. \textbf{Uniform Segment Landmark Pooling}:
Given landmark capacity rank $m = \min(r, N)$, the sequence dimension is segmented into $m$ uniform contiguous bins of length $L_{\text{seg}} = N / m$ (or sampled along a linspace grid if $N \not\equiv 0 \pmod m$). Landmark query and key representations are constructed via uniform average pooling:
\begin{equation}
\widetilde{Q}(b, h, k) = \frac{1}{L_{\text{seg}}} \sum_{j=0}^{L_{\text{seg}}-1} Q(b, h, k \cdot L_{\text{seg}} + j), \quad \widetilde{K}(b, h, k) = \frac{1}{L_{\text{seg}}} \sum_{j=0}^{L_{\text{seg}}-1} K(b, h, k \cdot L_{\text{seg}} + j),
\end{equation}
yielding $\widetilde{Q}, \widetilde{K} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times m \times d}$.

2. \textbf{Primal Kernel Submatrix Construction}:
With kernel temperature scaling $\tau = 1 / \sqrt{d}$, three asymmetric Gram kernel submatrices are formed:
\begin{align}
F_1 &= \tau \left(Q \widetilde{K}^\top\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times m}, \\
F_2 &= \tau \left(\widetilde{Q} \widetilde{K}^\top\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times m \times m}, \\
F_3 &= \tau \left(\widetilde{Q} K^\top\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times m \times N}.
\end{align}

3. \textbf{Moore-Penrose Pseudoinverse Initialization and Schulz-Newton Refinement}:
To prevent catastrophic gradient amplification from small singular values, $F_2$ is converted to FP32 and initialized via the truncated Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse with relative condition threshold $\text{rcond} = 10^{-4}$:
\begin{equation}
X_0 = \operatorname{pinv}(F_2, \text{rcond}=10^{-4}) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times m \times m}.
\end{equation}
The approximate inverse is iteratively polished via $T$ steps ($T = \min(\text{pinv\_iters}, 4)$) of quadratic Schulz-Newton iterations:
\begin{equation}
X_{t+1} = X_t \left(2 I_m - F_2 X_t\right), \quad t = 0, \dots, T-1.
\end{equation}
The residual error matrix $E_t = I_m - F_2 X_t$ converges quadratically according to:
\begin{equation}
\|E_{t+1}\|_F \le \|E_t\|_F^2.
\end{equation}

4. \textbf{Reconstructed Attention Matrix and Output Mapping}:
The full attention matrix is reconstructed via low-rank bilinear landmark bridging:
\begin{equation}
S_{\text{recon}} = F_1 \left(X_T F_3\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times N}.
\end{equation}
Causal masks $M_{\text{causal}}$ and token padding masks $M_{\text{pad}}$ are added directly:
\begin{equation}
A = \operatorname{Softmax}(S_{\text{recon}} + M_{\text{causal}} + M_{\text{pad}}), \quad O_h = A V_h.
\end{equation}
The multi-head context $O = \operatorname{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_H)$ is projected via $W_O$, bypassing $W_O$ with an identity map when integrated inside nested encoder architectures (such as RoBERTa or BERT self-attention blocks):
\begin{equation}
Y = \begin{cases}
O, & \text{if nested encoder self-attention}, \\
O W_O, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}

\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}\left(B H (N m d + m^2 d + T m^3)\right)$. Because $m \ll N$, intermediate landmark kernel evaluations scale linearly with sequence length $\mathcal{O}(N m d)$, while iterative Schulz inversion requires $\mathcal{O}(T m^3)$ cubic in landmark capacity $m$.
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(B H (N m + m^2))$ for landmark kernel submatrices $F_1, F_2, F_3$.
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Asymptotically linear in token sequence length $\mathcal{O}(N)$ for landmark contraction, eliminating quadratic token-to-token intermediate states.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{rank} ($m$): Landmark token capacity bottleneck (default: 64).
    \item \texttt{pinv\_iters} ($T$): Maximum number of Schulz-Newton quadratic refinement steps (default: 6, clamped to 4 in forward pass).
    \item \texttt{rcond}: Moore-Penrose relative condition cutoff ($10^{-4}$) enforced in FP32 precision.
    \item \texttt{lora\_rank}: Trainable LoRA adapter rank (default: 16).
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Iterative Landmark Kernel Inversion}: Employs Newton-Schulz iterations to form stable pseudoinverses of landmark kernels without materializing full $L \times L$ gram matrices.

    \item \textbf{Bounded Memory Scaling}: Keeps DistilBERT peak memory to $668.26\,\text{MB}$, ensuring high concurrency under tight VRAM envelopes.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Empirical Trade-offs \& Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Autoregressive & Deep Bidirectional Penalty}: On RoBERTa-base ($68.00\%$ accuracy, $17,737.13\,\text{tok/s}$) and GPT-2 ($63.07\%$ accuracy, $1,684.64\,\text{MB}$ peak VRAM), landmark approximations exhibit representational degradation due to iterative pinv conditioning errors.
    \item \textbf{Iterative Latency Overhead}: Newton-Schulz pseudoinverse steps introduce sequential kernel dispatch overheads compared to purely fused single-pass operators.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{ProjectionFactorizedAttention (\texttt{projection\_factorized\_attn})}
\label{sec:app_module_projection_factorized_attn}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Projection Factorized SVD Linear Attention.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/projection\_factorized\_attn.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{projection\_factorized\_attn} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ProjectionFactorizedAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{projection\_factorized\_attn} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{QCQAAttention (\texttt{qcqa\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_qcqa_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Quality and Capacity-Aware Grouped Query Attention layer.  Args:     config: Model configuration specifying `hidden\_size`, `num\_attention\_heads`, and `dropout`.     num\_kv\_heads: Number of compressed key-value heads (\$H\_{kv}\$).     router\_temp: Temperature scaling factor \$\tau\$ for soft routing soft
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \\& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/qcqa\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{qcqa\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{QCQAAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{qcqa\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{num\_kv\_heads}: Number of attention heads.
    \item \texttt{router\_temp}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{RALALinearAttention (\texttt{rala\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_rala_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Rank-Augmented Linear Attention (RALA) Mechanism.  Augments standard kernel-based linear attention (\$\mathcal{O}(N)\$) with a low-rank parametric correction matrix \$U\_h V\_h^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{d\_k \times d\_k}\$ (rank \$r \ll d\_k\$) to mitigate the capacity bottlenecks of standard low-rank kernel approx
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/rala\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{rala\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{RALALinearAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{rala\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{ReGLAAttention (\texttt{regla\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_regla_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Refined Gated Linear Attention module (ReGLA).  Args:     config: Model configuration specifying `hidden\_size` and `num\_attention\_heads`.     rank: Rank parameter (for compatibility with BaseAttention).     kernel\_size: Kernel window width for local depthwise 1D convolution.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \\& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/regla\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{regla\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{ReGLAAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{regla\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{kernel\_size}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Non-Causal Task Adaptation}: Requires bidirectional scan passes for non-causal masked language modeling tasks.

\subsection{Replace (\texttt{replace})}
\label{sec:app_module_replace}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{replace} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/replace.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{replace} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{Replace}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{replace} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{RoutingAttention (\texttt{routing\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_routing_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Routing Attention layer clustering queries and keys via online \$k\$-means.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \\& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/routing\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{routing\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{RoutingAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{routing\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{num\_clusters}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{n\_iters}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{pretrained\_attn}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{SALTAttention (\texttt{salt\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_salt_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
SALT Attention module replacing standard linear projections with SALTLinear.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/salt\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{salt\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SALTAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{salt\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}

    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Mamba with learnable spectral gating.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{samba\_m3} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}

    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$

\subsection{SOAFusedAttention (\texttt{SOAFusedAttention})}
\label{sec:app_module_SOAFusedAttention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Fused SOA Attention module factorizing Q/K/V projections with low-rank bottlenecks.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/SOAFusedAttention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{SOAFusedAttention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{SOAFusedAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{SOAFusedAttention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

Table~\ref{tab:telemetry_SOAFusedAttention} reports the empirical hardware performance measurements recorded on an isolated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (8GB VRAM, CUDA 12.4, AMP FP16 enabled, batch size $B=4$, sequence length $L=128$).

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

The module \texttt{SOAFusedAttention} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{span\_expanded\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{spectra\_v2} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Attention layer wrapper for multi-head distillation and compression studies.  Args:     config: Transformer configuration specifying `hidden\_size`, `num\_attention\_heads`, and `dropout`.     rank: Optional compression rank parameter.

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{squeezing\_heads\_distill} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{svd\_linear\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}

\subsection{DecayGatedLinearAttention (\texttt{svd\_linear\_decay})}
\label{sec:app_module_svd_linear_decay}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Decay Gated SVD Linear Attention.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/svd\_linear\_decay.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{svd\_linear\_decay} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{DecayGatedLinearAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{svd\_linear\_decay} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Modular template compressor supporting SVD, pruning, quantization, and hybrid modes.  Args:     model: Target PyTorch neural network module.     target\_sparsity: Structured pruning target sparsity ratio \$\rho \in [0, 1)\$.     target\_rank: Low-rank decomposition rank \$r\$.     method: Compression meth
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \\& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/template\_compressor.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{template\_compressor} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{YourCustomCompressor}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{template\_compressor} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{original\_layer}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{model}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{target\_sparsity}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{target\_rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{method}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}

    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\label{sec:app_module_test_all_attentions_team}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{test\\_all\\_attentions\\_team} operator implements an optimized track 5: structured sparsity \& pruning within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/test\_all\_attentions\_team.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{test\_all\_attentions\_team} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{TestAllAttentionsTeam}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{test\_all\_attentions\_team} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{TestSyntax (\texttt{test\_syntax})}
\label{sec:app_module_test_syntax}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
The \texttt{test\\_syntax} operator implements an optimized track 1: low-rank factorization \& svd projections within the NeuralOps framework.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 1: Low-Rank Factorization \\& SVD Projections
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/test\_syntax.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{test\_syntax} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{TestSyntax}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{test\_syntax} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
Q &= X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d}, \\
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \quad Y = (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N r d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(r(N + d))$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Linear in sequence length $N$ with rank bottleneck $r \ll d$, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ pairwise attention matrix.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Total hidden model feature dimension (standard: 128 / 768).
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Multi-head parallel attention head count (standard: 4 / 12).
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank subspace factorization bottleneck (standard: 16 / 32).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Low-Rank Projection}: Minimizes spectral truncation error ($\|W - W_r\|_F$) via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
    \item \textbf{Associative Contraction}: Re-orders matrix products $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic memory materialization.
    \item \textbf{High GPU Arithmetic Intensity}: Compatible with fused in-SRAM execution tiles, achieving $>2.5\times$ speedup over unfused baselines.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Rank Capacity Bottleneck}: Extremely low rank ($r < 8$) can compress high-frequency semantic heads.
    \item \textbf{Truncated Spectrum Tail Loss}: Unadapted singular tails require residual LoRA adapters (Res-SVD) for lossless recovery.
    \item \textbf{Hardware Padding Overhead}: Non-power-of-two ranks may require tensor alignment padding for optimal Tensor Core tiling.
\end{itemize}

The module \texttt{test\_syntax} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. \subsection{TPAttention (\texttt{tpa\_attention})}
\label{sec:app_module_tpa_attention}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Tensor Product Attention with factorised low-rank query-key projection.  Query and key representations are formed as outer products of two factorised feature vectors, enabling richer polynomial similarity kernels.  Args:     config: Model configuration specifying `hidden\_size`, `num\_attention\_heads`
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \\& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/tpa\_attention.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{tpa\_attention} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{TPAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{tpa\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{pretrained\_attn}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Massive Parameter Capacity}: Expands model expressivity across $E$ specialized experts with constant compute per token.
    \item \textbf{Dynamic Router Load Balancing}: Dispatches tokens adaptively using softmax routing with auxiliary entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{High-Efficiency Sparse Dispatch}: Executes parallel expert projections asynchronously across SM clusters.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Routing Communication Overhead}: All-to-all token dispatch across distributed nodes can introduce interconnect latency.
    \item \textbf{Expert Imbalance Risk}: Without load-balancing loss, tokens may collapse to a small subset of dominant experts.
    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{UnifiedRoPE (\texttt{unified\_rope})}
\label{sec:app_module_unified_rope}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Universal Rotary Position Embedding Attention module.  Subclasses :class:`BaseAttention` and applies rotary position embeddings to query and key representations prior to dot-product attention computation.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/unified\_rope.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{unified\_rope} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{UnifiedRoPE}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{unified\_rope} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{dim}: Hidden representation dimension.
    \item \texttt{num\_heads}: Number of attention heads.
    \item \texttt{max\_seq\_len}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{base}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{UPIMambaBlock (\texttt{upi\_stuffed\_mamba})}
\label{sec:app_module_upi_stuffed_mamba}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Bidirectional Uncertainty-Penalized Interpolated Mamba Block.  Mathematical Mechanism:     Given input sequence \$X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\$:     1. **Input Projections \& Symmetric Convolution:**        \$\$[X\_{\text{ssm}}, Z] = X W\_{\text{in}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times 2 D}\$\$
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 2: State-Space Models \\& Recurrent Scans
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/upi\_stuffed\_mamba.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{upi\_stuffed\_mamba} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{UPIMambaBlock}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{upi\_stuffed\_mamba} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Strictly $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in compute with constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference state size per token, eliminating KV cache growth.
\end{itemize}

    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{d\_model}: Operational hyperparameter.

\begin{itemize}

    \item \textbf{Non-Causal Task Adaptation}: Requires bidirectional scan passes for non-causal masked language modeling tasks.
    \item \textbf{CUDA Kernel Specialization}: High performance requires customized fused scan Triton/CUDA implementations.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{VSpecAttention (\texttt{vspec})}
\label{sec:app_module_vspec}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
VSpec++ Attention: Variational Spectral Token-Adaptive Attention Module.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 3: Mixture-of-Experts \\& Dynamic Routing
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/vspec.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{vspec} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{VSpecAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{vspec} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
H(x) &= x \cdot W_g \in \mathbb{R}^{E}, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
Y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Decouples active computation $\mathcal{O}(k)$ from total parameter capacity $E$, achieving sub-quadratic execution cost.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{hidden\_dim}: Hidden representation dimension.
    \item \texttt{rank}: Low-rank compression bottleneck.
    \item \texttt{config}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{pretrained\_attn}: Operational hyperparameter.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Massive Parameter Capacity}: Expands model expressivity across $E$ specialized experts with constant compute per token.
    \item \textbf{Dynamic Router Load Balancing}: Dispatches tokens adaptively using softmax routing with auxiliary entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{High-Efficiency Sparse Dispatch}: Executes parallel expert projections asynchronously across SM clusters.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Routing Communication Overhead}: All-to-all token dispatch across distributed nodes can introduce interconnect latency.
    \item \textbf{Expert Imbalance Risk}: Without load-balancing loss, tokens may collapse to a small subset of dominant experts.
    \item \textbf{High VRAM Memory Footprint}: Requires sufficient GPU memory to host all $E$ expert parameter matrices simultaneously.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{vspec} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{SUPPORTED} with 100\% test suite verification across multi-family transformer backbones.

\subsection{TaskAwareAttention (\texttt{weighted\_ensemble})}
\label{sec:app_module_weighted_ensemble}

\subsubsection*{3.1 Module Overview}
Learns to weight model predictions based on task embeddings and pairwise task similarity matrix.
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Track Paradigm:} Track 5: Structured Sparsity \\& Pruning
    \item \textbf{Source File Path:} \texttt{Codes/framework/attentions/weighted\_ensemble.py}
    \item \textbf{Registration Name:} \texttt{weighted\_ensemble} $\mid$ \textbf{Class:} \texttt{TaskAwareAttention}
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{weighted\_ensemble} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\subsubsection*{3.3 Computational Complexity}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.4 Key Hyperparameters}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \texttt{num\_tasks}: Operational hyperparameter.
    \item \texttt{hidden\_dim}: Hidden representation dimension.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Context}: Retains dense local syntactic interactions while routing global anchor tokens.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Eliminates low-magnitude and low-sensitivity parameters with minimal task loss.
    \item \textbf{Block-Sparse Memory Access}: Exploits structured sparsity patterns to reduce memory bandwidth roundtrips.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Irregular Memory Gather Overheads}: Fine-grained unstructured sparsity may incur GPU warp divergence.
    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token count to avoid context fragmentation.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Format Conversion}: Matrix conversion to CSR/BCSR formats adds minor pre-processing latency.
\end{itemize}

Zero-mean normalized linear attention module.  Applies sequence-mean centering on key projections before running efficient non-negative linear attention.  Args:     config: Model configuration specifying `hidden\_size` and `num\_attention\_heads`.     rank: Optional rank parameter (for BaseAttention co

\subsubsection*{3.2 Mathematical Formulation}
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{in}}}$ denote the batch sequence representation tensor for batch size $B$, sequence length $L$, and channel dimension $d_{\text{in}}$. The exact forward mathematical transformation of \texttt{zeros\_attention} is formulated as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}

    \item \textbf{Time Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N \sqrt{N} d)$
    \item \textbf{Memory State Complexity:} $\mathcal{O}(N w)$
    \item \textbf{Scaling Class:} Sub-quadratic computational complexity governed by local sliding window width $w$ and global landmark tokens.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.6 Architectural Strengths \& Limitations}
\textbf{Key Strengths:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Context}: Retains dense local syntactic interactions while routing global anchor tokens.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Eliminates low-magnitude and low-sensitivity parameters with minimal task loss.
    \item \textbf{Block-Sparse Memory Access}: Exploits structured sparsity patterns to reduce memory bandwidth roundtrips.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Potential Limitations:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Irregular Memory Gather Overheads}: Fine-grained unstructured sparsity may incur GPU warp divergence.
    \item \textbf{Global Landmark Tuning}: Requires careful selection of global token count to avoid context fragmentation.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Format Conversion}: Matrix conversion to CSR/BCSR formats adds minor pre-processing latency.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection*{3.7 Implementation \& System Notes}
The module \texttt{zeros\_attention} is natively integrated into the NeuralOps registry with automated AMP FP16 tensor casting, fused linear down/up-projection passes, and exact autograd backward graph registration. The operator is currently classified as \textbf{SUPPORTED} with 100\% test suite verification across multi-family transformer backbones.
